title: Baroreflex stimulation to localize blood pressure regulating brainstem nuclei in a single individual
summary:
Arterial hypertension is a common disease. More than 40% of the German population are affected. Despite the serious consequences for the cardiovascular system, we cannot find a cause for the development of hypertension in around 90-95%. 
Already in the last century the neurosurgeon Jannetta and his colleagues theorized that blood vessels pulsating against a particularly sensitive region of the brainstem could affect nerve cells at that site and, thereby, trigger hypertension. The presence of such a vessel-nerve contact can be treated surgically. Currently, however, it is not possible to distinguish with certainty between a harmless vascular-nerve contacts and a contacts that result in hypertension.
Thanks to major technical advances in the acquisition and processing of functional MRI images of the brain, it is now possible to identify blood pressure regulating regions in human brains without radioactive exposure. However, this has so far only been possible by measuring a relatively large group of people (about 20). In a preliminary study, we were already able to demonstrate this by increasing the blood pressure in the test subjects using a drug.
The aim of this study is to localize blood pressure regulating areas in a human subject without test medication, namely by reductions of the ambient pressure in the neck area (neck suction). The carotid arteries in this area contain blood pressure sensors (baroreceptors). The negative pressure causes the sensors to be stretched. This fake increase in blood pressure is then passed to the brain by a nerve signal. We assume that a sufficiently high number of repetitions of neck suction with different strengths allows to detect the activation of the corresponding brain regions in an individual person.
conditions: Healthy subjects and patients with autonomic dysfunction

interventions.name:
Suction at the neck = 0 mmHg
===
Interventional, controlled, randomized, open study. In N-of-1 studies, all measurement results originate from the same person. The number of intervention repetitions corresponds to the group size in traditional studies. Study conclusions relate to the investigated

Suction at the neck = -10 mmHg
This intervention will be applied to healthy subjects as well as patients. All participants represent their own control.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy subjects: Age ≥ 18 years. === Patients: Age ≥ 18 years, suspected neurovascular compression of the medulla near the root entry zone of the vagal 
nerve or autonomic dysfunction.
Exclusion criteria:
- Positive urine pregnancy test in women of childbearing age (premenopausal)
- Previous surgery or radiation in the carotid sinus region
- Afferent baroreflex failure
- Atrial fibrillation
- Valvular heart disease
- Carotid atherosclerosis with >50% stenosis cannot be ruled out by ultrasound
- MR exclusion criteria
- Metal implants or other osteosynthesis material, stents, clips etc., that are not MRI compatible or hinder examinations due t- their location
- Pacemaker, infusion pump, neuro-stimulator, inner ear implant
- Claustrophobia
- Permanent make up or tattoos which are not suitable for MRI
- Piercings that cannot be removed
- Current diseases of vital organs or central nervous system
- Psychiatric disorders which may hinder subjects in consenting or complying with the protocol
- Regular use of medicines with influence on the outcome of the study (hormonal contraceptives are no exclusion criteria)
- Regular consumption of alcohol (20-30 g/day) or drugs
- Blood donation within 3 months for women and 2 months for men before the study
- Clinically relevant findings in the ECG such as a second- or third-degree AV block, prolongation of the QRS complex over 120 ms or of the QTc-interval over 450 ms
- Supine hypertension (> 140/90 mmHg) or hypotension (< 90/50 mmHg)
